Income tax in India is a direct tax levied by the government on the annual income earned by individuals, businesses, and other entities. Taxpayers can file 
returns, check details, and make direct payments through the official Income Tax Department Portal.Tax Regimes and SlabsIndia has two tax systems: the Old Tax 
Regime (which permits many deductions and exemptions) and the New Tax Regime (which offers lower tax rates but fewer deductions). Under the New Tax Regime, income 
up to ₹4,00,000 is tax-free, with gradual slab increases up to 30% for income above ₹24,00,000. Income tax in India is a direct tax levied by the government on 
the annual income earned by individuals, businesses, and other entities. Taxpayers can file returns, check details, and make direct payments through the official 
Income Tax Department Portal.Tax Regimes and SlabsIndia has two tax systems: the Old Tax Regime (which permits many deductions and exemptions) and the New Tax 
Regime (which offers lower tax rates but fewer deductions). Under the New Tax Regime, income up to ₹4,00,000 is tax-free, with gradual slab increases up to 30% 
for income above ₹24,00,000.Heads of IncomeTaxable income is categorized into five distinct groups:Income from SalaryIncome from House PropertyProfits and gains 
from Business or ProfessionCapital GainsIncome from Other Sources (such as interest or dividends)
